key_insight: Nitrogen vacancies weaken polar-axis lattice coupling in wurtzite AlN, enabling defect-mediated switching whose spatial and temporal patterns govern ferroelectric domain growth.
engineering_relevance: Engineering nitrogen-vacancy distributions, aided by scandium doping, offers a route to lower coercive fields for low-voltage ferroelectric memory.
evidence_signal: Combined simulations and experimental characterization support vacancy-mediated nucleation and reconcile ideal-crystal predictions of polar-axis growth with experimentally observed lateral or nearly isotropic growth.
watch_item: The abstract does not quantify the vacancy-control window or device-level reliability trade-offs needed to translate reduced coercive fields into scalable memory.
paper_title: Nitrogen vacancy cluster-mediated ferroelectric domain growth in wurtzite AlN
